scenes.name: the two numbers, counted from the shapes
scenes.visual: Dark canvas, one continuous two-row ledger: prefill in the top half, decode in the bottom half, identical layout and one shared scale, so the rows compare directly. Frame 1920 x 1080; keep x < 420, y < 110 free for the chapter label. Left column, x 60 to 420, the inputs. Prefill: 2,000 blue token pills in a 40 x 50 grid, each pill 7 x 4 px at a 9 px column pitch and 6 px row pitch, so the grid spans x 60 to 420, y 190 to 490, with a grey tag '2,000 tokens' centred under it at y 515. Decode: one blue pill, 40 x 22 px, centred at (240, 740). Column x 450 to 520: a small stack of five blue weight tiles (60 x 36 px, each offset 3 px) beside each row's input, centred at (485, 340) and (485, 740); it stands for the weights in the memory beside the chip, and coral byte particles leave it along the bytes lane. Lanes: every bar starts at x = 600 and the full scale is 1,000 px (x 600 to 1600): 1,000 px is 290 trillion operations on an amber lane and 146 GB on a coral lane. Prefill row: heading at (60, 160); one-line equation at (600, 205); lane label 'operations' at (600, 248), amber bar y 265 to 295; lane label 'bytes moved' at (600, 343), coral bar y 360 to 390; grey sub-label, 20 px, right-aligned to x 1600 at y 418, so it spans about x 1180 to 1600; result pill left-aligned at x 600, centred on y 465, 44 px tall. Decode row: the same layout exactly 400 px lower (heading y 560, lane labels at (600, 648) and (600, 743), operations bar y 665 to 695, bytes bar y 760 to 790, sub-label y 818, result pill y 865). A fraction slot for each row sits at x 1000 to 1450 beside its result pill, 24 px text: numerator baseline y 462, fraction bar y 472, denominator baseline y 500 for prefill, and 862, 872, 900 for decode, so its top stays about 25 px below the sub-label; each row's sub-label dims or fades before its fraction builds. End tags are left-aligned at x 1615, at each bar's mid-height, and end before x 1880, except decode's operations tag, which sits by the magnifier. The magnifier: a small white ring of radius 12 round the hairline's start at (600, 680), a short leader line running right from it, and a disc of radius 50 centred at (780, 680), so x 730 to 830 and y 630 to 730, clear of both decode lane labels and of the decode bytes bar; the disc shows the hairline enlarged as a short amber stroke, and its tags sit outside it, left-aligned at x 845. Bottom band, centred at y 1000: one white summary line. Bar lengths, to scale: prefill 280 trillion is 966 px plus a lighter amber attention segment of 34 px, tagged schematic because its true share is 2 to 4 percent depending on how it is counted; prefill bytes are 959 px for 140 GB plus one hatched 41 px coral block for the extra 6 GB, drawn as a single schematic block, not split; decode's 140 billion operations are 0.48 px, a hairline shown through a magnifier; decode's 140 GB is 959 px, ending exactly under the prefill weights segment. Colour: operations amber, bytes coral, tokens and weights blue, text white and grey. Labels dim to 40% once they stop being the subject. The idea: two ratios counted from shapes, not measured; nearly identical bytes buy work that differs two-thousand-fold.

beats.say: Operations per byte, phase by phase. Prefill first: two thousand prompt tokens at a hundred and forty billion operations each, two hundred and eighty trillion. Attention adds a few percent, about two hundred and ninety trillion.
beats.show: On 'Operations per byte', two empty pill outlines draw where the result pills will land, left-aligned at x 600 and centred on y 465 and y 865, each holding a grey '? ops per byte'; on 'phase by phase', they pulse in turn, top then bottom, and dim to 40%. On 'Prefill first', the heading 'Prefill · 70B model · 2,000-token prompt' writes on at (60, 160). On 'two thousand prompt tokens', the 40 x 50 grid fills row by row in about one second and its tag '2,000 tokens' appears. On 'a hundred and forty billion operations each', one pill lifts out and passes through the weight stack, each tile flashing amber, while the amber equation writes on at (600, 205): '2 × 70 billion = 140 billion ops per token'. On 'two hundred and eighty trillion', the whole grid pulses, a wave sweeps through the stack, the equation morphs in place into '140 billion × 2,000 = 280 trillion' (one line, never two), the lane label 'operations' writes on, and the amber bar sweeps from x 600 to 966 px with end tag '280 trillion'. On 'Attention adds', the lighter 34 px segment clicks onto the end and a small grey tag, right-aligned to x 1600 under it at y 318, reads 'attention: a few %, schematic'; on 'about two hundred and ninety trillion', the end tag morphs to 'about 290 trillion'.

beats.say: Yet the weights cross the bus once, a hundred and forty gigabytes, plus about six for activations and the running record. About two thousand operations per byte.
beats.show: The equation and the attention tag dim to 40%. On 'cross the bus once', the lane label 'bytes moved' writes on, a single dense stream of coral particles runs out of the weight stack along the bytes lane, once, and the coral bar grows to 959 px, end tag '140 GB'. On 'about six', the hatched 41 px block clicks onto the end, the tag becomes 'about 146 GB', and the grey sub-label writes on under the bar: 'weights, plus activations and cache writes'. On 'two thousand operations per byte', the sub-label dims to 40%; then the two end tags fly into the fraction slot and stack, amber 'about 290 trillion' over coral 'about 146 billion bytes', and the fraction collapses leftward into the result pill, which replaces its placeholder: '= about 2,000 ops per byte', outlined amber.

beats.say: Decode, one request's next token: a hundred and forty billion operations, on the same hundred and forty gigabytes every time. The chip itself holds only about a tenth of a gigabyte.
beats.show: The prefill grid, stack and lane labels dim to 40% and its sub-label fades; its bars, end tags and result pill stay bright. On 'Decode', the heading 'Decode · one token · batch size one' writes on at (60, 560), and the decode lane labels 'operations' and 'bytes moved' write on at (600, 648) and (600, 743). On 'one request's next token', one blue pill drops in at (240, 740). On 'a hundred and forty billion operations', the decode amber bar grows to its true 0.48 px, effectively invisible; the magnifier's small ring circles it, the leader line draws, and the disc at (780, 680) opens on the enlarged hairline; the end tag 'about 140 billion' writes on outside the disc at (845, 672), and under it, in grey at y 702, 'drawn to scale: 1/2,000 of the bar above'. On 'the same hundred and forty gigabytes', a coral stream runs from the decode stack and the coral bar sweeps to 959 px, end tag '140 GB'; a thin white vertical guide joins its end to the end of the prefill weights segment directly above. On 'every time', the stream fires twice more, the bar flashing on each pass, and the sub-label 'the same weights, every time' writes on. On 'a tenth of a gigabyte', a small chip-outline icon pops up between the decode pill and the stack at (360, 805), with the grey tag 'chip holds ≈ 0.1 GB' centred under it at (360, 845), set beside the decode stack so the gap reads as 140 GB against 0.1; icon and tag fade at the end of the beat.

beats.say: Same model, same chip, both from the shapes alone: two thousand against one. Decode gets one operation from each identical byte.
beats.show: The magnifier's ring, leader and disc, all lane labels, sub-labels and the drawn-to-scale tag fade, and so do the grid, both stacks and the decode pill, so only the two headings, the bars with their end tags and the result pills remain. On 'from the shapes alone', the decode fraction builds in its slot: amber '2 × 70 billion' over coral '70 billion × 2 bytes'; the two 2s strike through each other, then the two 70 billions, and it collapses into the decode result pill, which replaces its placeholder: '= about 1 op per byte', outlined coral. On 'two thousand against one', both result pills pulse together and the white summary line writes on at y 1000: 'Same model, same chip: 2,000 against 1'. On 'each identical byte', the white guide between the two 959 px coral segments pulses, and the decode bytes bar fills with a fine row of coral byte-blocks, each topped by one amber dot.

scenes.name: both phases on the roofline
scenes.visual: Opens at t = 0 on the H100 roofline, rebuilt from ch11_s05's chart: a new shot after the title card, so it is built in its starting state, not morphed from ch11. Kept from ch11_s05: horizontal axis 'operations per byte (log)' along y 900, ticks 1, 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 at x = 320, 570, 820, 1070, 1320 (250 px per factor of ten); vertical axis 'trillion operations per second (log)', ticks 1, 10, 100 at y = 900, 650, 400 and no '1,000' tick, as in ch11 (also 250 px per factor of ten, so the slanted ceiling runs at exactly 45 degrees); plot clipped at y = 110, a clip on plot lines only, never on labels; amber flat ceiling at y = 151 (989 trillion); coral slanted ceiling through (320, 769) and (570, 519) up to the ridge at (938, 151); white ridge marker at (938, 151) with a thin white dashed vertical down to the horizontal axis; region tints at 10%, coral left of the ridge and amber right. Changed from ch11_s05: (1) the vertical axis line moves from x 320 to x 260, 60 px left of the intensity-1 tick (the axis now starts at about 0.58), so a dot at intensity 1 sits clear of it; the horizontal axis extends left to meet it, y tick labels are right-aligned to x 245, and the rotated vertical title is centred on y 450 at x 70. (2) Only the roof is drawn: the dashed slant beyond the ridge and the flat line left of it, dimmed in ch11, are gone. (3) ch11's two-line tag under the flat line's right end (x 1100 to 1310, y 190 and 225) would hit the prefill label, so it becomes one amber line '989 trillion/s', 20 px, left-aligned at x 1180 above the line at y 135, ending by x 1330, clear of the prefill-to-ridge bracket, which ends at x 1145. (4) ch11's 'the ridge' at (990, 195) becomes white 'ridge, 295' on the tick-label row at (938, 935), between the '100' and '1,000' ticks. (5) ch11's sidebar header 'the roofline · H100' and its rule are gone, replaced by a grey corner tag 'H100' at (340, 140), and the sidebar widens from x 1400 to 1820 to x 1400 to 1880 and starts empty. Added in this scene: workload dots, decode in coral at (320, 769) with label 'decode, intensity 1' to its lower right at (345, 795), prefill in amber at (1145, 151) with label 'prefill, intensity 2,000' centred just below it at (1145, 185). Sidebar: two horizontal gauges, each 340 px long from x 1400 to 1740 and 30 px tall, 'arithmetic busy' in amber with its label at y 300 and bar y 315 to 345, 'bus busy' in coral with its label at y 410 and bar y 425 to 455; each readout, 22 px, sits left-aligned at x 1760, right of its bar, and ends by x 1870. From b3, the 30 ms thesis bar from ch05, redrawn 440 px wide at x 1400 to 1840, y 620. Brackets that measure distance run along y 870, just above the horizontal axis, with their tags centred above them at y 855, except the prefill-to-ridge bracket, which runs above the flat ceiling at y 128 with its tag centred above it at y 108. The idea: two dots two thousand times apart on one axis, and where each sits says by itself which resource is idle.

beats.say: On the roofline, prefill sits about seven times right of the ridge: arithmetic flat out, bandwidth to spare.
beats.show: At t = 0 the chart stands in its starting state, with no dots, brackets or gauges. On 'prefill', the amber dot drops onto the flat ceiling at (1145, 151) with its label. On 'seven times', a white bracket at y 128 spans x 938 to 1145, its tag '× 7' centred above it at (1041, 108). On 'arithmetic flat out', the 'arithmetic busy' gauge fills amber, readout '100%'; on 'bandwidth to spare', the 'bus busy' gauge fills coral to '≈ 15%' and stops, the rest of it hatched grey.

beats.say: Decode sits nearly three hundred times left, low on the slanted ceiling: bus almost always busy, arithmetic under one percent.
beats.show: The '× 7' bracket fades. On 'Decode', the coral dot drops onto the slanted ceiling at (320, 769) with its label; a 60 px white dotted line runs left from it to the axis at x 260, and a coral read-out tag '3.35 trillion/s' writes on at the dot's height, right-aligned to x 245 at y 775, between the '1' and '10' tick labels. On 'nearly three hundred times', a white bracket along y 870 spans x 320 to 938, tag '× 295' centred above it at (629, 855). On 'bus almost always busy', the gauges switch to decode: 'bus busy' fills coral to '≈ 100%'; on 'under one percent', 'arithmetic busy' drains to an amber sliver, readout '0.34%'.

beats.say: That's where the ninety-nine percent went. Nothing is broken: the workload's shape leaves the chip able only to wait.
beats.show: The gauges and the '× 295' bracket fade. In the sidebar at y 620, the thesis bar from ch05 returns, 440 px wide from x 1400 to 1840: a 2 px amber sliver tagged 'arithmetic, under 1%' and the rest coral, with a small stopwatch icon reading '30 ms' above its left end. On 'ninety-nine percent went', a white label writes on over the coral part: 'waiting for weights'. On 'able only to wait', a small hourglass icon settles on the decode dot and the coral tint around it deepens from 10% to 25%.

beats.say: Two points, two thousand times apart. Almost everything ahead tries to move the left one rightward.
beats.show: The thesis bar and the hourglass fade; only the axes, the two ceilings, the ridge and the two labelled dots remain. On 'two thousand times apart', a white bracket along y 870 spans x 320 to 1145, tag '× 2,000' centred above it at (733, 855). On 'move the left one rightward', a teal arrow grows out of the decode dot up along the slanted ceiling toward the ridge, and holds.

scenes.name: the hard throughput ceiling
scenes.visual: A new composition: decode's position turned into a speed limit. Centre-right, the GPU package illustration: an amber compute die, 260 x 260 px, centred at (1250, 560); two coral-outlined HBM stacks, 90 x 220 px, centred at (960, 560) and (1540, 560); between each stack and the die a wide bus channel along which coral particles flow at one steady speed. A thin ring of radius 175 around the die fills coral as particles arrive; each full ring stands for one complete 140 GB crossing, after which a blue token pill pops out of the die, arcs left into an output tray at x 140 to 620, y 520 to 600, and the ring resets. Cadence is slowed for readability: one ring every 1.2 s, about 29 times slower than the real 41.8 ms, with a small grey tag 'slowed down' left-aligned at (1460, 412), up and right of the ring and clear of it; the counter 'tokens per second' under the tray at (380, 680) always shows the true rate. Top band: an equation centred on y 200, 36 px, that builds term by term and carries into the next scene, each term with a fixed centre: blue 'max tokens per second' at x 400, white '=' at x 640, coral 'bandwidth' at x 790, white '÷' at x 930, coral 'bytes per token' at x 1130. The numbers that replace the coral terms morph into the same slots, and the white-outlined result box '≈ 24 tokens/s' sits at x 1360 to 1620. Below the equation, y 255 to 295, a row for three grey condition chips, 20 px text, centred at x 790 ('this chip', under '3.35 TB/s'), x 1020 ('16-bit weights', under '140 GB') and x 1290 ('one token per read', under 'per token'), each joined by a thin grey line up to its term; the chips arrive only in b3, after everything else in that row has gone. Top-right callout slot x 1380 to 1880, y 260 to 380, on two rows: a stopwatch icon with '≈ 30 ms per token · H200' at y 290, 20 px; and a formula at y 345, 24 px. Bus label, from b3: 'the limit: how fast the bus delivers weights', 22 px, centred at (1250, 800) under the package. Colour: bytes and bandwidth coral, the token rate blue, the die amber. The idea: the token rate is a flow divided by a fixed load, and nothing inside the die can change it.

beats.say: Decode's top speed is bandwidth over bytes per token: the thirty-millisecond division, flipped. On an H one hundred, pretending the model fits, three point three five terabytes a second over a hundred and forty gigabytes: about twenty-four tokens a second.
beats.show: The package draws on, coral particles start along both channels and the ring begins to fill. On 'Decode's top speed', the bus channels brighten while the die stays a dim amber, and blue 'max tokens per second' lands at the left of the equation row. On 'bandwidth over bytes per token', the rest of the equation builds term by term, each landing on its word: white '=', coral 'bandwidth', white '÷', coral 'bytes per token'. On 'thirty-millisecond division', the callout appears in the top-right slot: the stopwatch with '≈ 30 ms per token · H200' and, under it in coral, 'bytes ÷ bandwidth'. On 'flipped', that formula turns over in a half turn to read 'bandwidth ÷ bytes', and a white curved arrow draws from it to the equation's 'bandwidth ÷ bytes per token'. On 'pretending the model fits', a grey tag writes on under the equation's left end, centred at (400, 270): 'H100: a what-if, needs 2 chips'. On 'three point three five terabytes a second', 'bandwidth' morphs into '3.35 TB/s'; on 'a hundred and forty gigabytes', 'bytes per token' morphs into '140 GB per token'. On 'twenty-four tokens a second', the result writes on in the white-outlined box at the equation's right, '≈ 24 tokens/s'; blue pills start popping into the tray, one per ring, and the counter runs to '23.9' and holds.

beats.say: A physical ceiling, not a software one: no cleverer kernel beats it, since even instant arithmetic waits for bytes.
beats.show: The callout, its curved arrow and the what-if tag fade. On 'no cleverer kernel', the die flashes amber, a grey tag beside it reads 'faster kernel', and an amber readout on the die counts 'arithmetic: 0.14 ms' down to '0 ms'. On 'waits for bytes', the particles keep exactly their speed, the ring fills at the same pace, the next pill emerges only when it completes, and the counter stays at '23.9' with a grey 'no change' beside it.

beats.say: It bounds every serving system on this chip, with sixteen-bit weights and one token per read: the most one answer can stream, and the most the chip can make.
beats.show: The kernel tags fade. On 'every serving system', the bus channels glow coral and gain the label 'the limit: how fast the bus delivers weights' at (1250, 800), and a horizontal ceiling line locks across the top of the tray at y 520, tagged '24 tokens/s max' just above it at (380, 505). On 'this chip', the first grey condition chip, 'this chip', appears at (790, 275), joined by a thin line up to '3.35 TB/s'. On 'sixteen-bit weights', the second, '16-bit weights', appears at (1020, 275), joined to '140 GB'. On 'one token per read', the third, 'one token per read', appears at (1290, 275), joined to 'per token'. On 'the most one answer can stream', the tray's ceiling line pulses; on 'the most the chip can make', the counter '23.9' pulses.

scenes.name: the only three ways past it
scenes.visual: Continues straight on from the ceiling, no cut. The package, tray, counter, bus label and 'slowed down' tag fade out. The top band slides up 45 px as one group, unchanged in form and x positions: the equation 'max tokens per second = 3.35 TB/s ÷ 140 GB per token' with its result box '≈ 24 tokens/s', now centred on y 155, and the three grey condition chips, now centred on y 230 at x 790, 1020 and 1290, still joined to their terms. Header 'The only three ways past it', white, 32 px, centred at (960, 80), above the equation, so no connector line crosses it. Three teal cards, 520 x 440 px, at x 120 to 640, 700 to 1220 and 1280 to 1800, y 340 to 780: 'Raise bandwidth' over 'a different chip'; 'Shrink bytes per token' over 'lower precision, compression'; 'Amortise the transfer' over 'batching, or several at once'. Each card joins with a thin teal line from the centre of its top edge, (380, 340), (960, 340) and (1540, 340), up to the bottom of the condition chip it changes, at y 250; the three lines do not cross, and that chip's own line to its term turns teal with it. Each card's lower 280 px holds a small worked example. Card 1: three horizontal bars to scale at 7 px per token per second, grey 'H100 · 3.35 TB/s' 168 px '24/s', teal 'H200 · 4.8 TB/s' 240 px '34/s', teal 'B200 · 8 TB/s' 400 px '57/s'. Card 2: a coral stack to scale, 200 px for 140 GB, halving to 100 px '70 GB' and 50 px '35 GB', with readouts '8-bit: ≈ 48/s' and '4-bit: ≈ 96/s'. Card 3: one coral read arrow fanning out to ten blue pills in slightly different shades, the line '140 GB ÷ 10 = 14 GB per token', a bracket '≈ 240 tokens/s' with a grey 'weights only' tag, and a separate pill that splits into three. As each card fills, the previous card's worked example dims to 40%, so at most one example is bright. Bottom band, y 860 to 1000: a teal path and one closing white line. The idea: the three ways out are exactly the three conditions under the equation, so the roadmap falls out of one line.

beats.say: Only three ways past it, one per condition. Raise bandwidth: a different chip. Or shrink the bytes: eight-bit weights give about forty-eight a second.
beats.show: On 'Only three ways', the header writes on and three card outlines draw. On 'one per condition', a teal line draws from each card up to its chip, and that chip's grey line to its term turns teal: card 1 to 'this chip' and '3.35 TB/s', card 2 to '16-bit weights' and '140 GB', card 3 to 'one token per read' and 'per token'. On 'Raise bandwidth', card 1 fills with its title and sub, and its bars grow in turn: the grey H100 reference, then H200 and B200 in teal, readouts '24/s', '34/s', '57/s'. On 'shrink the bytes', card 1's example dims and card 2 fills; on 'eight-bit', the 200 px coral stack '140 GB' halves to '70 GB', readout '8-bit: ≈ 48/s'; at the end of the beat it halves again to '35 GB', readout '4-bit: ≈ 96/s'.

beats.say: Or amortise each read: ten batched requests make about two hundred and forty a second, counting the weights alone, each still at twenty-four. A later trick amortises within one answer: several tokens per read.
beats.show: Card 2's example dims and card 3 fills. On 'ten batched requests', one coral read arrow fans out to ten blue pills in slightly different shades, one per request, and the line '140 GB ÷ 10 = 14 GB per token' writes on. On 'two hundred and forty', a bracket round all ten reads '≈ 240 tokens/s'; on 'counting the weights alone', the small grey tag 'weights only' attaches to it. On 'each still at twenty-four', every pill gets a tiny '24/s'. On 'A later trick', a separate blue pill appears at the card's right edge with the tag 'several at once · later'; on 'several tokens per read', it splits into three pills of one answer, all fed by a single coral arrow.

beats.say: Each gets its own video. One line of arithmetic, three escape routes: the entire roadmap.
beats.show: All three worked examples fade, leaving the card titles and subs. On 'its own video', a small film-strip icon drops onto each card in turn. On 'One line of arithmetic', the equation at the top glows once. On 'three escape routes', the three teal connector lines pulse together, from the cards up to the chips. On 'the entire roadmap', a teal path draws beneath the three cards from left to right, and a white line writes on under it at y 960: 'three escape routes: the entire roadmap'.

checks.claim: Operations per token = 2 × 70 billion = 140 billion (decode, and each prefill token)
Prefill weight operations for a 2,000-token prompt = 2 × 70e9 × 2,000 = 280 trillion
Attention cost per query-key pair across the model (QK and softmax×V, 2 ops per multiply-add, 128 head dim, 64 heads, 80 layers) = 2,621,440 ops; reproduces fig 115's 5.4 GFLOP at 2,048 context

Attention inside a 2,000-token prefill adds 5.2 trillion (causal, 1.9%) to 10.5 trillion (full square, 3.7%): said as 'Attention adds a few percent' and tagged 'a few %, schematic' on screen, since the drawn 34 px segment cannot state which count applies
280 trillion plus attention = 285 to 290.5 trillion, so the atlas's 'about 290 trillion' is consistent
'Attention adds a few percent, about two hundred and ninety trillion': 290 against the spoken 280 trillion is +3.6%, inside the 1.9% to 3.7% range above
Extra prefill bytes beyond the weights: 146 - 140 = about 6 GB

Reconstruction (not stated in the atlas, and dependent on fusion assumptions) of the ~6 GB: residual activations read+written per layer 2,000 × 8,192 × 2 B × 2 × 80 = 5.24 GB, cache writes 2,000 × 327,680 B = 0.66 GB, total with weights 145.9 GB. Because it is a reconstruction, the film draws the 6 GB as one schematic block labelled 'activations and cache writes', not as a measured split
Prefill intensity: 290 trillion / 146 billion = 1,986, 'about 2,000'; without the extras 280 trillion / 140 billion = exactly 2,000
Decode intensity: (2 × 70e9 ops) / (70e9 × 2 bytes) = 1 op per byte; the 2s and the 70 billions cancel

CORRECTION (reviewer blocker): the chip holds 'about a tenth of a gigabyte' (132 SMs × 512 KB + 50 MB L2 ≈ 0.12 GB), not 'a few hundred kilobytes' for the whole chip; matches ch02_s02 b3 and ch09_s01 b4. 140 GB is ≈ 1,150 times that
Prefill about seven times right of the ridge (2,000 / 295 = 6.8); decode nearly 300 times left (295 / 1); the two dots 2,000 / 1 = 2,000 apart
Decode attainable = 1 op/byte × 3.35 TB/s = 3.35 trillion ops/s = 0.34% of the 989 trillion peak ('under one percent')

s02 b3 'ninety-nine percent': on the H100, decode's bus time is 1 - 0.14 ms / 41.8 ms = 99.66% of each token (the 0.34% gauge's complement); on the H200 it is 99.51%, so the callback to ch00 and ch06 holds on either chip
Same sliver as the 30 ms thesis bar from ch05: 0.1 / 30 = 0.33%
Prefill at peak: arithmetic 290e12 / 989e12 = 0.29 s; reading 146 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 43.6 ms; bus busy 14.9%, gauge '≈ 15%'
Decode on H100: arithmetic 140e9 / 989e12 = 0.14 ms; reading 140 GB / 3.35 TB/s = 41.8 ms

Decode on H200: 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms, the 'thirty milliseconds', spoken once in this chapter, in s03 b1 ('the thirty-millisecond division, flipped', echoed by ch18_s03 b1), with the stopwatch callout '≈ 30 ms per token · H200' over 'bytes ÷ bandwidth'. s02 b3 is on the H100 chart, so it says 'ninety-nine percent', not 'thirty milliseconds': the H100's 295 and 0.34% are never tied to the H200's 30 ms (ch18_s01 b3 makes that distinction)
Hard ceiling on H100: 3.35 TB/s / 140 GB = 23.9, said in full as 'about twenty-four tokens a second', paying off ch02_s05 b4's promise and matching ch13_s11 b2
H100 is a what-if for this model: 140 GB needs 2 of its 80 GB chips
Raise bandwidth: H200 4.8 TB/s / 140 GB = 34 tokens/s; B200 8 TB/s / 140 GB = 57 tokens/s
Shrink bytes: 8-bit weights 70 GB give 47.9 tokens/s; 4-bit 35 GB give 95.7 tokens/s on 3.35 TB/s
Amortise: ten requests share one read, 140 GB / 10 = 14 GB per token, 3.35 TB/s / 14 GB = 239 tokens/s in total, shown and said as 'about 240'; each user still 23.9/s (weights only)

s01 bars at 1,000 px full scale (290 trillion ops, 146 GB): 280 T = 966 px, attention 34 px, 140 GB = 959 px, 6 GB = 41 px, decode's 140 billion ops = 0.48 px; ops ratio 290e12 / 140e9 = 2,071, tagged '1/2,000 of the bar above'
s02 roofline in ch11's coordinates (x = 320 + 250·log10(intensity), y = 900 - 250·log10(ops/s / 1e12)): decode (320, 769), ridge (938, 151), prefill (1145, 151)
checks.python: import math; X=lambda i: 320+250*math.log10(i); Y=lambda p: 900-250*math.log10(p/1e12); print(round(X(1),1), round(Y(3.35e12),1), round(X(989/3.35),1), round(Y(989e12),1), round(X(2000),1))

checks.claim: s02 vertical axis line at x = 260, 60 px left of the intensity-1 tick, sits at intensity 0.58
